To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have annotated the pig genome for ncRNAs and identified a number of ncRNAs in pig that are unique for Laurasiatherians, and that we have identified a number of de novo RNA locus with conserved structure in pig and other vertebrates.
we have annotated a large number of structured RNAs of which a large fraction is novel.

(1) We have annotated 3,556 RNA loci, 1,004 of which are lineage specific, (2) 528 RNA loci are novel miRNAs and 1,581 are pseudogenes, and (3) 83,859 RNA loci were predicted with de novo methods, of which 528 overlap with the homology-based and novel miRNA annotation.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the following aspects: 1) the development of a comprehensive annotation of ncRNAs for the pig genome, 2) an assessment of the reliability and completeness of the annotation, and 2) the identification of de novo ncRNA candidates.
the annotation of structured RNAmolecules in the porcine genome, which is of great importance for the pig as an animal model for human diseases and for production.
two aspects of ncRNAs in the pig, their annotation and their evolutionary conservation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our annotation represents our best current effort, and that we believe that the majority of our structured RNA loci are true positives, but that we are aware of some false positives.
the pig genome is well annotated for structured RNAs, but the annotation is far from complete.
the RNA annotation is of very high quality and that we are able to provide the community with a reliable and detailed annotation of the structured RNAs in Sus scrofa.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the pig genome holds 3,556 ncRNAs, of which 1% are lineage specific and 1% are de novo RNA locis predicted by RNAz.

1) the pig genome holds 4,439 structured RNA loci, 2) 3,556 loci are annotated, 3) 1,581 of the 3 556 annotated loci are pseudogenes, 4) 1,004 of the 4,439 loci are lineage specific and 5) the annotation of the pig genome is 99.9% reliable.

we have obtained a high quality annotation of structured RNACs in the pig genome, which is available in Ensembler and the complete annotation can be downloaded at http://r th.dk/resources/rn aannotator/ sussc r 102/version1.0 2.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a combination of homology based and de novo prediction of structured RNAs is a viable strategy for annotating structured ncRNAs in mammalian genomes, and the pig genome in particular.
a conservative annotation strategy, based on homology and structure similarity search, is sufficient for the annotation of structured RNAts.
the annotation of structured ncRNAs in mammalian genomes is possible, and that the annotation can be made available to the research community at a reasonable cost.
